text: Each request is assessed separately against the threshold.
Supplier names can be duplicated across different suppliers.
Emergency purchases above EUR 5,000 are exempt from Finance approval.
Supplier name uniquely identifies every supplier.
Multiple related requests are automatically merged into one request.
Emergency purchases must be reported to the board every Friday.
Different supplier records can share the same contact email.
A changed bank account must be checked independently before the next payment.
A buyer may activate a blocked supplier.
The buyer performs identity verification.
Identity verification must use a passport rather than another identity document.
Unchanged identity data must be certified by an external notary.
Automatic payment requires a purchase order and a receipt record.
A variance greater than EUR 10 prevents automatic payment.
A service invoice with service acceptance does not need a purchase order.
An analyst must request a corrected invoice for every blocked invoice.
The tolerance is increased by 5 percent for overseas suppliers.
An analyst must request corrections through a supplier portal.
For a purchase below EUR 5,000, the department manager may approve it, but is not obliged to do so.
A risk score below 70 is classified as low risk.
For a service invoice, an authorised service acceptance replaces the goods receipt record.
The Compliance officer performs identity verification and the buyer does not perform identity verification.
For any purchase whose amount is above EUR 5,000, Finance approval must be obtained before the purchase order for that purchase is issued.
An invoice is eligible for automatic payment only if both an existing purchase order and a receipt record are present.
A requester is prohibited from approving their own purchase request.
An invoice number must be unique only within a supplier; different suppliers may reuse the same number.
An approval expires 365 calendar days after its approval date.
For a blocked invoice, an Accounts Payable analyst may request a corrected invoice but is not obliged to request one.
The purchase threshold applies separately to each request and does not apply to the monthly total for a supplier.
Every new supplier must have identity verification completed before its first purchase order.
The tolerance is assessed per invoice, not against the monthly sum of a supplier's invoices.
Different suppliers may share the same supplier name, and supplier name is not a unique identifier.
Any new supplier must complete identity verification before its first purchase order.
The retention period begins on the approval date, not on the purchase order date.
For a low-risk supplier, Compliance may request a site visit but is not obliged to request a site visit.
For any blocked invoice, an Accounts Payable analyst may ask for a corrected invoice but is not obliged to ask for a corrected invoice.
